tagline: Seven places to stand in, from a Tokyo backstreet in the rain to Griffith Observatory after sunset.
description: Pocket Atlas is a globe with a pin on each place it holds. Pick a pin and you stand there. The camera tours the place by itself, and the stick takes over when you want to walk and look around.

There are seven places: a 24-hour convenience store on a Tokyo backstreet in the rain, the stone stairs below Suga Shrine in Yotsuya, Radio Kaikan in Akihabara at blue hour, the Enoden crossing at Kamakura-Kōkōmae with Sagami Bay behind it, Sangubashi No. 3 crossing in Yoyogi under cherry blossom, Lombard Street in San Francisco, and Griffith Observatory above Los Angeles twenty minutes after sunset. Each keeps its own hour and weather. A train passes Sangubashi about once a minute and Kamakura every two.

It runs on PS Vita, PSP, Nintendo 3DS, iPod touch and Android, with a renderer written for each device's GPU. A PS Vita, a 3DS and an Android phone have all seven places, an iPod touch has five and a PSP has two.
The browser version draws the PS Vita build's places inside the shell of any of four handhelds. The places need a desktop browser with WebGPU.

media.caption: Rainy Night Konbini: a 24-hour shop on a Tokyo backstreet, its light on the wet road, Tokyo Tower at the end of the street.
Sangubashi No. 3 crossing, Yoyogi: the lamps flash, the arms come down, an eight-car local passes and the arms rise.
Kamakura-Kōkōmae: an Enoden train comes along Route 134 and crosses the foot of the slope road, with Sagami Bay behind it.
Griffith Observatory twenty minutes after sunset, with downtown Los Angeles and the basin's lights below.
The stone stairs below Suga Shrine in Yotsuya, on a summer afternoon.
Radio Kaikan in Akihabara at blue hour, its signs lit.
Lombard Street, San Francisco: the brick turns and the hydrangeas between them.
The atlas screen's globe turned to Japan, with a pin on each place and the cities' lights on the night side.
